Amazon Q extension prompt injection

Target: Amazon Q Developer for VS Code · website · repo
Date: 2025-07-25
Actor: Third Party (group)
Target Kind: plugin
Language: TypeScript
Cause: compromised_credentials
Motive: malicious
Transitive: false
Impact: none
User Impact: 0
Phase: source

Synopsis

A threat actor used an overbroad GitHub token in AWS CodeBuild to commit malicious prompt-injection code into Amazon Q Developer for VS Code 1.84.0. The code shipped through the official extension release, but a syntax error prevented execution.

Story

AWS investigated the Amazon Q Developer for VS Code extension in July 2025 and found that its CodeBuild configuration exposed a GitHub token with too much repository access. AWS's AWS-2025-015 bulletin says the finding came from the related AWS-2025-016 CodeBuild investigation and that the token let the attacker commit code into the extension's open-source repository.

The malicious change was automatically included in Amazon Q Developer for VS Code 1.84.0. It targeted the assistant's code-context path rather than a normal binary payload: the injected content acted as a prompt intended to make the agent perform destructive local and AWS actions.

AWS said the malicious code was distributed with the extension but did not execute because of a syntax error. ReversingLabs and later case-study writeups framed the incident as a near miss because Amazon Q can operate with local files and cloud resources available to the developer.

AWS published AWS-2025-015 on July 23, 2025 and updated it on July 25, 2025. AWS revoked and replaced credentials, removed the malicious code, removed 1.84.0 from distribution channels, and released 1.85.0. Existing 1.84.0 installations still contained the inert malicious code, so AWS directed customers to remove 1.84.0 from use and update to 1.85.0, including forked or derivative copies.
